summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of heart surgery was admitted after presenting with diabetic ketoacidosis and elevated cardiac enzymes indicating a non-ST elevation myocardial infarction. She had no chest pain but was found to have new severe left ventricular dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 19%. A stress test revealed fixed perfusion defects, and cardiac catheterization showed significant coronary artery disease, leading to stent placement in multiple vessels. She was treated for DKA with insulin, managed for acute systolic heart failure with dialysis, and started on dual antiplatelet therapy. A small, asymptomatic arteriovenous fistula was incidentally found and deemed non-interventional. Cellulitis of the right index finger was treated with IV antibiotics, transitioning to oral doxycycline. Her condition stabilized, and she was discharged home with medication adjustments and follow-up plans.
problems: Acute on chronic combined systolic (congestive) and diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Arteriovenous malformation of vessel of lower limb
